title: What If Jupiter Disappeared?
description:
Jupiter has more than twice the mass of all the other planets combined. It is so heavy that the Sun and Jupiter circle a shared balance point that sits just outside the Sun's surface, so the Sun wobbles in a small loop every 12 years. If Jupiter vanished, that wobble would stop, and its moons (more than 90 of them) would no longer be held, so they would carry on around the Sun on paths of their own. Earth would not notice that night, but Jupiter (with Venus) drives a 405,000-year cycle in the shape of Earth's orbit that helps set the rhythm of the ice ages, so that slow climate beat would change. Whether we would be safer from asteroids is still argued about: Jupiter flings some comets away and sends others toward us.

Sources: NASA Jupiter facts; NASA on the Sun-Jupiter barycentre; Kent et al., PNAS (2018), the 405,000-year orbital cycle; Horner & Jones (2008), Jupiter: friend or foe?
Narration is AI-generated (ElevenLabs) and the pictures and opening clip are AI-generated. This is a thought experiment.
